replies:
Hi Robin! Here's how to set up a VLOOKUP recipe to pull values from one board into another:

1. **Install VLOOKUP Auto-link** from the monday.com marketplace and add it as a board view on your **target board** (the one where you want the data to appear).

2. **Create the VLOOKUP recipe:**
   - Choose your **target board** (where data should appear)
   - Choose your **source board** (where data comes from)
   - Select a **key column** that both boards share — like a dropdown or text column (e.g. Item ID, Project Code, Employee Email)
   - Choose the fields you want to sync from source to target

3. **Enable auto-link on item creation** so the lookup triggers automatically whenever a new item is created on the target board.

The key idea is that VLOOKUP matches items across the two boards using a shared key value, then pulls the corresponding fields over — no manual copying needed.

Full walkthrough here: https://jetpackapps.io/vlookup-auto-link/connect-and-sync-boards-easily-with-vlookup-on-monday-com/

Let me know if you run into any issues setting it up or if you have questions about which key column to use!

replies: Hi Robin! I'd be happy to help with your VLOOKUP questions. Let me pull up some info first — what specifically would you like to know? For example, are you asking about setup, how a particular feature works, or running into an issue?

Yes — VLOOKUP Auto-Link can connect boards across workspaces. All pricing plans include "Unlimited users & workspaces," so there's no hard limit on how many workspaces you can use it in.

One thing to note: licensing is **per workspace**. So if you're managing multiple workspaces, you'd need a plan for each one. You can see the details here: https://jetpackapps.io/monday-com-vlookup-auto-links-connect-boards-mirror/

What else did you want to know?

VLOOKUP is actually designed as a **replacement** for mirror columns rather than something that works alongside them. Mirror columns in monday.com are read-only and can't be used in formulas, automations, filtering, or reporting — VLOOKUP solves exactly that problem by pulling data into native columns instead.

So with VLOOKUP you get synced data that's editable, works in formulas, supports automations, and handles sub-items — all things mirror columns can't do. You can read more about the comparison here: https://jetpackapps.io/vlookup-auto-link/still-using-mirror-columns-in-monday/

What's your next question?

Yes — VLOOKUP fully supports subitems. You can connect subitems to items or even to other subitems across different boards, and there's a dedicated Subitem Sync feature you enable during setup. You can sync subitem details like status, due dates, and assigned team members just like regular items.

You can read more about how it works here: https://jetpackapps.io/vlookup-auto-link/sync-items-and-subitems-seamlessly-across-multiple-boards-in-monday-com/

Anything else you'd like to know?

VLOOKUP's sync is event-driven rather than on a fixed schedule. When you set up activation triggers (like "when item is changed" or "when item is created"), the sync fires in real time whenever those events happen on either the source or target board. So there's no set interval — it updates as changes occur.

You can read about the available triggers here: https://jetpackapps.io/vlookup-auto-link/set-up-activation-triggers-for-vlookup-to-sync-updates/

title: Embedded inside the customer's monday account
rubric: On the monday surface the account is known and reliable. She should use it rather than asking the customer which account they are on.
replies:
Hi Robin — VLOOKUP recipes require the user creating them to be an **account admin** with edit/write permissions on the boards involved. This is called out in our setup guide here: https://jetpackapps.io/setting-up-vlookup-2-0/

The key thing is that monday.com's "owner" role at the board or team level isn't the same as being an account admin. If your team owners don't have account-level admin rights in monday.com, they won't be able to create or manage VLOOKUP recipes and triggers.

One thing worth noting from our troubleshooting guide as well: even after a recipe is created, it runs under the permissions of the user who set it up — so if that person's access changes later, the recipe can stop working. That's why we recommend setting up recipes with a stable admin account: https://jetpackapps.io/vlookup-auto-link/how-to-fix-vlookup-authorization-issues-in-monday/

Can you confirm whether your team owners have account-level admin rights in monday.com? That'll help me point you to the right fix.
